These are the calls I'll run. First, the deferred-item schema and the current backlog, so the items match its format and the append doesn't clobber anything:

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/<deferred-backlog reference>
Read specs/deferred_items.md        # append if it exists; create if not
```

Then append this section, adjusted to the schema's exact field names:

```markdown
## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-07

- [ ] Closure email notices to boat operators (was Stage 2, Track B)
      Boat operators get an email within an hour of a lock closing, by polling the closure log about every 10 minutes. Text-message notices were left out with no owner.
      Size: small
      Done when: a notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every address on the list within an hour of a new closure-log entry.

- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (was Ranked list A #1, O2)
      Apply the Stage 1 closure-vs-gauge curve (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md: under 2% of days below 3.1 m, about 60% at 3.8 m) to the river-level forecast. That is one model run a day.
      Size: small (Stage 1's fit took 22 min on a laptop)
      Done when: each lock has a 7-day closure-risk outlook from the river-level forecast, recorded with its measured run cost.

- [ ] Pooled per-lock closure curves for all 14 locks (was Ranked list A #2, O3)
      Stage 1 fit one curve, and the four longest-record locks looked close to it.
      Size: medium (about 14x Stage 1's 1.8 GB; a few hours of fitting if cost scales linearly from 22 min)
      Done when: separate closure curves for all 14 locks, pooled across locks, are fit on real data and recorded with their measured run cost.

- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (was Ranked list A #3, O4)
      One static map page of each lock's closure history.
      Size: about a day
      Done when: boat operators can open a map showing each lock's closure history.
```

Then retire the roadmap and commit:

```
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
# insert under the title:  > PARKED (2026-11-07) — 1 of 2 stages complete
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap (1 of 2 stages complete): funding ended"
```

Nothing else retires with it. This roadmap came from new-project entry with no spec, so there are no methodology or critique files. Stage 1's findings file and plan 4 stay where they are, and the O2 and O3 items cite them.

I'll report the commit hash once it's done. Nothing is handed off.
